A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAGE and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. All 18 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and the inference algorithm, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAGE segmentation results, component ablations, attention analyses, efficiency measurements and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds style-reference sensitivity results in Table 7.

M1.justification: The style-prompt generators, adaptive fusion, losses, backbone and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Testing different style sets does not introduce a new method component; the added parallelization statement does not specify a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Table 7 expands the auxiliary training styles beyond lakeside, pier, valley and volcano to include ambulance, shark, barometer, can opener, snorkel and tennis ball. The five segmentation datasets and source-to-target tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Baseline, Full Fine-Tuning, IBN-Net, IW, DRPC, ISW, GTR, SAW, A2XP and FAMix comparators. Full Fine-Tuning scores change, but comparator membership and the described comparison methods do not.

E3.justification: The new Table 7 evaluates 12 style combinations with three to six prompts under the Cityscapes-to-other-domains protocol. Existing reported splits, preprocessing, metrics and training settings are retained; no protocol revision explains the changed Full Fine-Tuning scores.

E4.justification: Section 10.2 and Table 7 add sensitivity analysis of style-reference identity and number. The existing generator-type, initialization, attention-component and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point performance estimates and the same attention-weight boxplots. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; its phrase 'significant gains' introduces no statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all Full Fine-Tuning performance entries: average mIoU for GTA V, Cityscapes and SYNTHIA training changes from 32.76/39.22/26.31 to 39.14/41.07/35.98. SAGE remains at 42.09/43.90/37.58, substantially narrowing its reported margins; Full Fine-Tuning now exceeds SAGE on GTA V-to-BDD and Cityscapes-to-SYNTHIA. Table 7 additionally reports style configurations with average mIoU spanning 35.60–43.90.

T1.justification: Equations 1–36 and the mathematical formulation in the supplementary theoretical details are unchanged. No theorem, proof, derivation or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same novelty, adaptation and performance claims. The introduction foregrounds the gradient-access requirement, but this condition already appeared in v1's limitations.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets Table 7 as demonstrating robustness to style selection and no further gains beyond four styles. It also attributes style-count-independent latency to parallelization, without corresponding timing measurements and despite retaining a sequential-generation description in Section 8.3. Existing limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes prompt generation and fusion as parallelized. This changes implementation documentation, but its conflict with the retained sequential description prevents treating it as a verified implementation change. Existing checkpoint, architecture, optimizer, hardware and resource details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added and five removed. Additions include collaborating foundation models for DGSS and several adaptation or remote-sensing studies; removals include the MaaS survey and encrypted-segmentation references. The main positioning within style augmentation and visual prompting remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the introduction, brings the existing gradient requirement into the main text, updates corresponding-author information and adds acknowledgements. Appendix sections and cross-references are renumbered, while the overall narrative and organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, revises Table 3's grouped header and caption, and adjusts headers and formatting in Tables 5–6. Figures retain their substantive content, with limited repositioning and surrounding page reflow.

improvement.justification: Table 7 provides useful evidence about style-selection sensitivity, and the introduction makes an existing gradient requirement more visible. However, the new robustness interpretation is difficult to reconcile with the 35.60–43.90 mIoU range, and the constant-latency claim lacks measurements and conflicts with the sequential inference description. The substantial Full Fine-Tuning score replacements are also unexplained. These gains in transparency and unresolved evidential inconsistencies prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
